html:
A Finnish company that began as a paper mill in 1865 and, around the year 2000, became the world's largest maker of mobile phones.

The mining engineer Fredrik Idestam set up a wood pulp mill in southern Finland, then part of the Russian Empire, and soon moved it to the town of Nokia, which gave the firm its name. In 1967 it merged with a rubber company, maker of boots and tyres, and a cable company. It made everything from toilet paper to televisions.

In the 1980s and 1990s Nokia bet on mobile networks and phones as Finland's old trade with the Soviet Union collapsed. Europe's shared mobile standard helped it, and by 1998 it sold more phones than anyone. At its peak it was a large share of the whole Finnish economy.

The arrival of the touchscreen iPhone in 2007 and Android phones caught it out. In 2014 it sold its phone business to Microsoft. Nokia lives on as a maker of mobile network equipment.
sum: A Finnish company that began as a paper mill in 1865 and, around the year 2000, became the world's largest maker of mobile phones.
